text: {"answer": "The evidence is mixed and depends on context. A randomized trial at Ctrip found a 13% performance increase for fully remote call center workers, attributed to fewer sick days and a quieter environment [d658dc380b73#6]. A later study from Bloom and co-authors reportedly found fully remote work reduced output by 10-20% for some roles, particularly those requiring high collaboration or newly hired workers [d658dc380b73#6]. A meta-analysis summary reports a median productivity impact of +10% for focused tasks and -4% for collaborative tasks [d658dc380b73#5]. Another study found full-remote work (five days a week) was associated with reduced work productivity, while promoting remote work reduced stress responses [abefd158b9c2#2]. A field experiment found discretionary remote working of about two days per week helped mothers without harming non-mothers [ef88116f982d#0]. Overall, remote work is not uniformly positive or negative for performance; it depends on how organizations provide autonomy, connection, and support [47cdadbd2ab4#2].", "confidence": 60, "one_line": "Mixed evidence: remote work can raise productivity for focused tasks and some workers, but fully remote work can lower it for collaborative roles."}
